tips.comment: Valor Spirit can go well for the Richard Fahey yard. Valor Spirit has got a first start today but has a very good pedigree and is bred for speed. Can go well today for a stable that gets juveniles to win first time out.
Slightly weak in the market but Exactly Right has the profile here to build on the last win on the all weather to score here on the turf. Great chance.

Rogue Diplomat has run to third for both runs so far, with the latest being when stepping up in trip to 1m2f and a bit further away. I don't think that today's drop to 7f is a bad thing, so worth a chance with Harry Davies this time.
Finished well back in the Jersey Stakes at Ascot last time but had displayed exceptional form in a novice prior to that, even in defeat. Solid claims.

Just the one run in the flats in the UK when 5 of 7 at Redcar last July. But hoping the trainer has worked on a few things in the last 8 months, and the same class and distance might just give her the stability to cause a huge upset tomorrow.

Gincident’s been out of sorts lately, but he’s fallen a long way in the weights and is now looking really well treated compared to that strong third off 80 at Newcastle in October. This could be the right time to catch him, and if he bounces back even close to that level, he’s got a big chance of getting back on track.
Another Baar has raced better on good ground than quite a few of these and although not always convincing, could put it all together here to win.
He's Got Game can go well for the Hugo Palmer yard. He's Got Game has won over this trip before and has run at Kempton this season. He will need that run and can do better with that race to work on.
Won from 3lb lower mark on AW 2 runs back and then not seen to best effect last time. Back to turf today and has a favorite's chance in this.
Has been performing well and, despite not fully delivering on promise when beaten by a neck off a mark of 72 at Wolverhampton last time, is a big player.

Saturnalia’s been holding his form nicely and was only just denied at Lingfield last time, beaten three-quarters of a length off 70. He ran to a similar level on turf last summer, so switching surfaces shouldn’t be an issue. In this sort of mood, he looks sure to be right in the mix again.
Probably not as effective on grass, but has won over the trip previously and does arrive here in excellent, consistent form from the all-weather, so could have an each-way shout.

Beelzebub was in decent form last summer and went off well backed on his last start when beaten 4 lengths at Nottingham. He’s got the ability to be competitive off this mark, but the long layoff does bring a fitness question. That said, there’s been some overnight support, which suggests he might be ready to go.
CHARLIE MASON looks to be in the peak of form and has every chance to take advantage of a favourable draw and race profile to take care of this. Looks the one to beat.

Raft Up’s been in solid form lately, showing a good attitude to win at Newcastle and then backing that up well last time despite the 3lb rise. She’s clearly thriving and with the yard faring well in turf handicaps (115 runs, 27 wins, 24% strike rate, +89pts @ 78% ROI), she should be right there again if holding her form.

Gemini Star signed off last season with a strong third at Redcar, showing she can mix it at this level. She's well-handicapped and represents a yard that does well with fresh horses. If ready on return, she has the ability to swoop late and steal this.
Performed to expectations, finishing just three-quarters of a length behind off a mark of 83 over 10 furlongs in AW. Now, with a favorable mark, it can win this.

Ciara Pearl looked good when winning at Newbury on testing ground and backed that up with a solid run in Listed company. She’s back from a break and now on a career-high mark, but she’s clearly going the right way and still has more to offer.

Expert Witness made a solid return for her new yard, posting an eye-catching RPR of 98. If she sees out the trip, she has the class to make a serious impact. With that recent run under her belt, she could surprise a few at decent odds.

Afloat was consistent last season at Yarmouth in October and was placed in 3 of her 5 other starts. She was beaten just 3.75 lengths in a Class 2 handicap at Doncaster on her last start, so she must have a good chance off 1lb lower in a Class 4.

Fireblade didn’t get his head in front in novice company but showed enough, especially when third at Kempton in January behind a next-time-out winner. Now switching to handicaps for a new yard with a good jockey booked, there’s a fair bit to like. Could take a step forward and go well at a nice price.
8-time winner who has gone 7 races without a win but is now on the same mark as when last winning. Can be slow away but holds an each-way chance if finding best form.
Consistent performer who has won on 2 of the last 5 starts. Up 2lb for the latest win and should go well again. Likely to be there or thereabouts.
James Doyle hangs around till the last race in the day to ride What's In The Bag, who remains relatively unexposed and also has shown real ability on faster ground. Good chance.

Was Superb winning at Southwell last November, but has been well beaten in the last 2 starts since (both on AW). So perhaps a switch back to turf might be beneficial for him. He's no mug on turf, and going down in class should help.

It remains to be seen how Handstands will perform on faster conditions at Aintree. He won his only point and won his first hurdle race on good going. This season, switching to fences, he fell in his first chase but has then been unbeaten in his last three races: two Grade 2 novice chases and last time a battling short-head win over Jango Baie at Sandown in a Grade 1 novice chase. He could win again.
Caldwell Potter has to be my choice as he returned from a short break to a G2 win last month by over 6L on GS. He gets my vote as I am a Harry Cobden fan, and I would expect a run from the front.

Dancing City is an experienced 8-year-old gelding trained by Willie Mullins. He has 7 out of 12 wins and 2 out of 3 in chasing. Things didn't go to plan at Cheltenham, but when assessing the manner in which Dancing City won his first two chases, it suggests it would be reasonable to draw a line through that Cheltenham form. He is ground versatile and likes this track, having won the Sefton Novices Hurdle over 24.5f last year. Dancing City can get back on track today under Paul Townend.

Has won 4 of his 7 starts up to 2m4f, the last one on penultimate start in a Beginners Chase at Gowran back in January. Was running well in a Grade 1 over 3 miles at the Cheltenham Festival until unseating 4 from home after a jumping mistake. Still open to improvement for the in-form Mullins yard and could be each-way value with a good round of jumping.

A good 2nd place finish in the Brown Advisory at Cheltenham. If that race hasn't taken too much out of him, he can go close again. Usually held up off the pace and could be suited by the long straight at Aintree.
The Changing Man has not been bad since returning from the last break in November with one win in G2 and four seconds in G3 out of six runs. He can handle the going and the trip EW.

Jordan was 4l behind yesterday's winner Impaire Et Passe in December and shaped as if further would suit. Then ran another good race when staying on at Cheltenham. Today's step up in trip could bring more out of the 8yo, and if that last run after a 75-day break brings him on, he has fair claims.

Don't Rightly Know represents the stable of Polly Gundry. Very different horses are the favorites in this race. But let's think about this a little bit. Don't Rightly Know has a 7lb advantage as a mare. She has won all three chase races she has entered. Remarkably, those were her last three races. So there is every reason to assume a successful performance from her in this prestigious race at Aintree.

Another trainer who tends to target his runners at this race, having won this 3 times in the past. He ran a cracker in the Coral Cup last time out, sporting the first-time cheekpieces. He travelled into the race like the winner but was eventually run down late on by another of Willie Mullins' handicap good things in Jimmy Du Seuil. No disgrace there given that horse was massively chucked in off his handicap debut mark. The handicapper has reacted accordingly, shoving him up 4 lbs for that run, which means he must shoulder top weight in this race. His overall form would suggest he should be able to cope with the rise in the weights. He won well enough on his penultimate run at Newbury, again travelling into the race like a good thing, recording a nice easy win in the end. If he repeats that run and the Coral Cup run, he's probably the one to beat here if the weight concession isn't a problem for him.

Handicapper has left his mark untouched for the last run. To be fair, he stood little chance being ridden out wide throughout. Still, he travelled into contention before his run petered out. I still think he's well in off this type of mark based on his overall form. The trainer has saddled 2 of the last 3 winners of this race, so knows what it takes to win this event. His run behind Burdett Road in the Greatwood rates the standout piece of form. He was only beaten 1/2L by that horse. That form got boosted with Burdett Road finishing 2nd in the Champion Hurdle a few weeks back. If he repeats that form here, that would give him decent claims.
Olly Murphy continues in fine form and Wade Out has always looked a horse of some promise. He looks to have got in this competitive race from a fairly lenient handicap mark and could go very well.

This horse was backed off the boards to land the ultra-competitive Martin Pipe race at the end of the Cheltenham Festival but flopped there. However, it is still unexposed and is clearly thought to be much better than that. I suspect early mistakes ruined his confidence, and maybe the 'lesser' jockey didn't give the horse the best ride on the day. So he's well worth another chance with Mark Walsh now in the saddle. For any horse to go off as short as 5/2 in the Martin Pipe on his fifth start, you'd have to say he's very highly thought of. Any horse is usually worth forgiving for one poor run, so the 13/2 is well worth taking.
Upped in trip today to 2m 4f. Up in the ratings but continued to improve last time out at Sandown. Each way player in this big field.

A 5-time winner whose last win came in the Scottish Champion Hurdle in April of last year. Bit so good in 3 starts since, but could find more for this step up in trip and rates an each-way player with 6 places.

Tintintin is a 6-year-old gelding trained by Fergal O'Brien. 10/38 wins of late is 4/15 wins over hurdles and largely campaigned over 16f. But given performance in the Imperial Cup last time when beaten a length suggests today's 20f should now be suitable. Towards rear, pushed along and still plenty to do before 2 out, headway from 2 out, ridden run-in, kept on and went fourth final strides over 16f - interesting runner for a bang in form yard!
Unexposed, improving horse who came 2nd on its handicap debut at Uttoxeter on soft ground last time out. Can progress again here.

A trappy race for me with two last time backed at the top of the market, but I’ll take a chance on Helnwein all the same. A venture chasing hasn’t gone to plan, but he’s run with credit mostly, and no more so than chase debut when running into a now 148 rated animal giving plenty of weight away. He’s beaten some of these on worse terms when last seen over hurdles, and whilst this step up in trip is an unknown, he was 3rd in a point behind Croke Park, and breeding would indicate he should get further than the trips he’s tried so far. Two of his three wins have come in fields of 17 or more, so he should be at home in this hustle and bustle.

Had a bit to find with the best of these but looks well handicapped especially with the 7lb off and can hit the frame despite looking stable second string. Was fifth in the mares bumper at this meeting last year but that was a decent race and my fancy should go well as will love decent ground. Taken well to hurdles winning first three starts and though only fourth the last twice should go well returning to this flat track on decent ground. Caught my eye when rallying last time behind my later fancy Jet To Vegas and has a good place claim here.

Steel Ally was a good second by a neck in a G2 under Dylan Johnson last time out and goes again with the same rider but claiming 3 lbs this time. So although up 2 lbs for that second, I think the claim could keep him thereabouts again. EW 6P.

Blenkinsop was absent for 659 days after running in a three-mile Grade 1 novice hurdle at this Meeting in 2023 but looked to be coming back into form in his second race back at Uttoxeter last time when 3rd of 15 over this distance, beaten less than five lengths. If he comes on again for that run, he could go close at 50-1.

Off The Jury showed improvement on first completed start since wind surgery when touched off in a competitive race at Sandown 27 days ago. This looks slightly tougher, but he is only 6 years old and there could be more improvement to come. He gets good ground and went well here last year. Owner/rider knows the horse well and no surprise if he is bang there at the finish again.
This looks like being a wide open race and with 6 places up for grabs I can see some good value with Hansard who is a multiple winner on this going, and placed in the race before last.

Minella Missile is very well weighted on the best of his form. He has lost his form somewhat this season, but carries a low weight, and if anywhere near the level of ability when beating Captain Teague, he could make a mockery of these huge odds.

Race 2 at Aintree today is the William Hill Handicap Hurdle (Premier Handicap) (Class 1) for 4-year-olds and upwards over 4,023 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 8-year-old gelding Serious Operator from the Lucinda V. Russell yard, and will be ridden by P.W. Wadge. This son of Malinas has a peculiar form line. Since winning at his third attempt, he then ran below form, then won, then way below form, then won, then below form twice, then won, then below, then won, and last time out way below. In hindsight, today looks like a win day for Serious Operator and is highly recommended for wagering concerns.

Last win was in April 2024, which saw the rating rise to 135 from 124. The win also was on good (good to soft in places). The rating has steadily come down to 129 today, so he shouldn't be a 50/1 shot each way, paying 6 places with conditions to suit.

Tune In A Box is a 6-year-old gelding trained by Tom Lacey. He has 4 wins out of 12 over hurdles, is ground versatile, and a distance winner but stays further, having won over 24f. He opened on a handicap mark of 85 and is now rated 127, some 42lb higher, so clearly has been a very progressive horse. Tom Lacey fits first-time cheekpieces, and since 2020, Tom has had 11 winners from 38 and 20/38 places with horses in first-time cheekpieces. His Tune In A Box could go well today, and this big field shouldn't hold any fears, having won a 24-runner field at Punchestown last April by 8l.
Form figures when running off 131-133 of 1,2,1,2. This is an admittedly tougher race, but with the extra places available, he's a big enough price to have a go at to at least run into a place.
Massive price available for Beacon Edge, who will enjoy the firmer ground and is a proven horse at this level (and higher) - shouldn't be this big.

Not exactly a great price for this race, but I feel he's a solid choice given he ran a cracker in the Supreme Novices last time out. That race is usually a good prep for this one, with 9 of the last 12 winners of this running in the Supreme prior to coming here and taking this race. He's proven to be a useful horse this season. Form figures 1213. Winning his maiden on hurdling debut with any amount in hand. He managed to win the Grade 1 Paddy Power Novices on his penultimate run, beating stablemate Bleu De Vassy with any amount in hand. As mentioned above, he finished 3rd in the Supreme last time out. He ran very well, just couldn't match the finishing speed of the front two. He did stay on nicely enough, however. If he repeats that form here, he's the one to beat for me. He's a confident selection.

Impressive in the Dovecote at Kempton and although now needs to step up he has the potential after just 4 hurdles runs. Hurdles quickly and travels well within and I think can be involved contention today.

Salvator Mundi is a young 5-year-old gelding trained by the irrepressible Willie Mullins. He didn't quite get it right in the Supreme Novice Hurdle at the Cheltenham Festival but took a keen hold early, which didn't help matters. He finished unplaced in the Triumph Hurdle the year before, so maybe Cheltenham is not his thing. Previously, he won two races posting RPR of 146-139, the former a 62-length romp. He is out of an unraced dam who was related to three, two of which won, notably the Alan King-trained L'Unique rated 149, who incidentally won a Listed and Grade 1 hurdles at Aintree. So today's track could potentially be right up Salvator Mundi's street, and he should go well under Paul Townend.

Diva Luna won a bumper at this meeting last year, but her only hurdles win so far was in a maiden hurdle against geldings at Cheltenham on New Year's Day over two and a half miles. She finished 3rd of 23 last time at the Cheltenham Festival in a Grade 2 mares' novice hurdle over two miles one furlong. Could at least get a place, getting her seven-pound mares' allowance.
Hasn't finished outside the first two home in his five career runs so far, including winning his last two outings, the latter in a Grade 2 over 2m 2f 25yds. Today's drying ground will suit.
Beaten 10 lengths latest. Jumped poorly and did too much too soon. Now had wind operation. Place claims with very good jockey Dan Skelton aboard.

Danny Mullins rides Karbau for in-form trainer Willie Mullins. He won a race at Punchestown in January quite impressively and recorded a fast time figure in the process. Disappointing in the Supreme Novices' Hurdle last month but was out the back early after a slow start. Likely is better than that and is a tasty each-way price here at 40-1.
This horse has done nothing but improve this season. He beat 2 decent performers last time out at Newbury and looks a huge each way price.
Jonbon can hopefully bounce back from his unlucky run at Cheltenham where a bad mistake cost him the race. He has got a very good record at Aintree and the step up in trip should be no problem.

El Fabiolo has met Jonbon three times, with Jonbon holding on in a photo finish over hurdles here in 2022. At the Cheltenham Festival the following year, El Fabiolo won the Arkle from Jonbon by over five lengths despite a mistake at the last. Since making it seven wins in a row in the Grade 1 Dublin Chase in February 2024, Fabiolo's jumping has been problematic, and he lost out to Jonbon at Sandown through mistakes in 2024. The Mildmay Course at Aintree is a less demanding jumping test, and if El Fabiolo gets round with only one minor mistake, he could have too much pace for Jonbon at the finish.

Protektorat will need to be at his best to win this. Harry Skelton will have only one plan, and that will be to make all like he did at Windsor. With only 4 runners on perfect ground, the C/D winner looks value.

A chance is taken with a 7-year-old gelding trained by Nigel Twiston-Davies and owned by top owners Simon Munir & Isaac Souede. He is class winning 5/16 races and is 3/10 chasing. He won on his penultimate start at Windsor, posting a career-high RPR of 166, so he's in his prime and being 7 years old has loads of scope. He slammed Unexpected Party in that contest by 10 lengths (received a whopping 10 pounds too), a two-time Cheltenham Festival winner who finished 2/20 in the Grand Annual Chase at this year's Cheltenham Festival, posting a career-high RPR of 150. Sans Bruit was 19.75 lengths behind in that contest, and he won this week's Close Brothers Handicap Chase at Aintree this week for the second consecutive year. Matata is rated 5-8-9 pounds behind his three market rivals, which isn't a great deal, and Matata could well surprise being the youngest in today's party of four.

Blue Lord has three grade one wins back in 2022 and I do think Willie Mullins favourite is on a dangerous mark today in the Topham Handicap Chase. Third in February at the Ascot Chase and I think Blue Lord will be ridden to victory by Paul Townend.

EXCELLO is interesting as a Nicky Henderson trained chaser who looks well treated at the base of this handicap chase. The cheek pieces are fitted and this six year old boasts some early career winning form over fences in France which can serve him well. Possibly a plan by connections and no real surprise if he were punted.

Bad represents Ben Pauling's stable. He has three wins on his record. Remarkably, he has won his last two races at Kempton, showing great form in the process. These wins make him one of the main contenders for the win, as the last two winners of this race have won after their victories in the previous races. At the very least, the chances of a podium finish look very strong.

Sits just 1 lb above the mark he ran off when finishing a solid 2nd in this race last season. He ran a cracker in this last season. Enjoyed every minute of this demanding course. Looked to have them all at it jumping the final fence before he was run down late on by Arizona Cardinal. Beaten just 1L. His campaign has been geared around a repeat run in this race. Finishing out the back of the tele on a number of occasions. I felt his most recent run showed some promise, however. Not beaten all that far in 5th place. Paul Townsend jumps off and rides Blue Lord this time, having ridden him in this event last year. To be fair, I'd rather side with the one we know handles this demanding track rather than back an unknown quantity. He's got solid claims of going one better this time around with JJ Slevin in the saddle.
Ginny's Destiny showed signs he was coming back to form at Cheltenham last time. His front-running style and brilliant jumping look tailor-made for this race.
The runner-up effort last time was very good considering the horrible mistake he made. He still has every chance if he manages to avoid that.

Won a Class 2 last October, staying on well at the finish of 2m 3f 98yds. Rating went up to 136 from 132 and has run respectably in three races since. Could have an excuse for the last outing as he was upped to 3m 1f, which he didn’t see out. Back down in trip today on drying ground, which suits.

The Goffer looks well handicapped on a mark of 137 and tends to come in for plenty of market support usually. Has won over this trip in the past at Grade A level at Leopardstown. Ran well to finish fourth in the Cross Country Chase at Cheltenham last time out. Good jumper who could easily take to Aintree's fences. Gordon Elliott trained 8yo rated as high as 149 in the past gets the vote in a fiercely competitive and exciting Topham Handicap Chase.

Marble Sands is usually ridden by a conditional, but the stable jockey is on board now for the first time since being on for the horse's last win. That looks significant since the horse has been given a chance by the handicapper here. He races off 143 and won off 146 for that last win for this jockey, which was over virtually the same trip and ground as he gets here today. The stable couldn't be any hotter either, with 6 of their last 8 runners winning, which is an incredible purple patch for them.
These fences might be the making of him. His mark is a fair one having already been placed from this mark. The ground is also a plus. I expect this one to go well at a price

The trainer makes no secret that they have targeted this race for 2 years (after being taken out when found lame last year). Lounge Lizard has jumped these fences well enough previously and will get his favored ground. With a six-place payout, he offers some Each Way value.
Do think that Latenightpass takes the eye in this lineup, with this horse regularly taking on the largest obstacles. So the Grand National fences will be no issue here. Good each way chance.

A 4-time winner whose last win came in a handicap chase over 2m4f at Cheltenham last November. Not so good the next twice but ran well enough over an inadequate 2m1f trip at Leopardstown last time out in early February. Has had a short break and goes well fresh. The stable's runner here yesterday ran well when 4th to Lossiemouth, so could go well at big odds.
Winner of two hurdle races and one chase and with the stable being in such great form it might be worth taking a chance on a decent priced contender here.

Not really a strong candidate for win purposes, admittedly. But boasts decent enough each-way claims in this wide-open affair. She loves this track. She also ran a cracker in this event back in 2023. A shade unlucky in defeat. She was hampered by a loose horse, causing her to lose vital momentum at a crucial stage of the race. She was beaten just over 1L by the winner back in 2nd place. The ground is key to her. She prefers faster going, but to be fair, she can go on softer ground also. Her best form has come on quicker going, however. She's vulnerable for win purposes, admittedly. But is a nice enough price to chance each-way in the hope she can hit the frame with 6 places up for grabs with ground and track to suit.
Jumped very well last time at Navan in a Grade 2 and should improve again for stepping up in distance. Should be positive and is too big at 33/1 and a good each way option.

This one has run at the Cheltenham Festival twice, falling in 2024 and was well beaten 15/20 in the Grand Annual this year. It is not often that horses who run well at Cheltenham can repeat the feat here, so a chance is taken that this one will show his best form on his first visit here. A small E/W at 22/1 would be a value bet.

The going is spot on for GA Law. Although an outsider, he has run in the best races against the best horses, so his lack of a win for over 400 days is no surprise. He is slipping down the handicap, so we have a chance to make some decent money on him. He is back at a distance that suits, so fingers crossed.
Eldorado Allen ran well for a long way in last year's Grand National before weakening late on. He is now lower in the weights, and the drop in distance looks ideal.

The 8yo has a progressive profile. Five runs this campaign, below par in two soft ground races but solid efforts in three good ground races. He lost by a nk in a Grade 2 on his return during Nov, similar trip and going as this handicap - the form boosted by the winner since. He was a Grade 2 winner during Dec. He was beaten a length last month in an £8K handicap, which looked like a fitness run and he’s in good shape. Every chance off his current handicap mark.

Shows some good form figures against other horses in this race. 1 win and 2 places from 7 runs in this class, 3 wins and 3 places from 17 chases. The going will suit today and each way chance at 50/1.

A few years since the last win and not the most consistent. You would have to say high risk, and 25/1 or bigger would be right. Did catch my eye late on, finishing well in a hot race at Cheltenham despite being hammered at the same track previously and has now finished well in the last 2 races. It is hard to fathom, but the going could be a plus, and if he takes to this track and fences, he has a long run in here to play catch up.

Has run really well in a pair of cross-country chases this season without getting home. These fences will be fine for him and there are plenty of pace angles liable to make this a proper test at the trip which should also be a help.

A 5-time winner who ran out an impressive winner over 2 miles at Carlisle on seasonal return last October. Finished second and third after that before running well to 3 out in the Grand Annual at last month's Cheltenham Festival. Could improve for this step up in trip and races prominently, which is often an advantage in this race over these fences, so may be good each-way value with 6 places.

I'm taking a chance on the Donald McCain-trained Minella Drama. The 10-year-old Flemensfirth gelding will love the ground and does well here at Aintree with a win in a Grade 2 over 20f back in Oct 24, as well as 2 places from 5 runs. He comes here fresh, and with conditions that suit, there are worse 40/1 shots out there.

Mister Meggit runs here fresh from comfortably winning his only hurdle race here over two and a half miles back in November. He can also erase the disappointment of being a beaten favourite here in the bumper at this meeting where he stumbled three furlongs out and could not recover.

Steps up in trip for the first time under rules, which is a wise idea given his P2P form. He's proven to be a solid horse over hurdles, winning 2 of his 3 runs. He won in a hack canter on hurdling debut. Admittedly, it wasn't a deep race, but he was most impressive. He bumped into the high-class The New Lion next time out, beaten 3L by the winner. No disgrace there given that horse went on to Turners at the festival. He's now 4/4 under rules. He got himself back into the winner's enclosure last time out, finding plenty for pressure to land a listed race, beating No Questions Asked by 1/2L. He showed great battling qualities to get back up and deny the runner-up. That last run hinted at a step up in trip being what he needs. He looks a stayer, all stamina. This is a step up on anything he's done to date, but he looks the type to progress now stepped up in distance.

Two wins from two starts since switching to hurdles this season, including when landing a Grade Two at Haydock last time out, stepping up to three miles for the first time. Goes on any ground and looks to have strong claims of completing the hat trick here today.

Familiar Dreams looks to have a great chance for Gordon Elliott in this Grade 1 Novice Hurdle. She has won 7 of her 15 starts on the flat and over hurdles, winning a Grade 3 at Limerick in her last start three weeks ago. It's possible the ground could be a bit quick, but she has won on good/yielding ground and looks a good each way bet with 4 places on offer.

Argento Boy is a 6-year-old gelding trained by Willie Mullins and ridden by Paul Townend. He has been a bit hit and miss in four hurdle starts but has plenty of ability. He won his maiden hurdle by 15 lengths and in two starts finished runner-up behind The Big Westerner (received 7 lbs), who has since gone 1-2, the latter in the Albert Bartlett at 9-2f. If Argento Boy can bounce back from a disappointing race in the Albert Bartlett, he could hold every chance.

This 3m PTP winner has looked improved on the last 2 starts when stepped up to 2 1/2 miles, winning a Grade 3 LTO at Naas, being strong at the finish. On the penultimate start, beat the Turners 4th, Forty Coats.
Moon Rocket won its first two starts over hurdles in impressive style. It has gone close since then and is now tried in first-time cheekpieces.

Connections of JULIUS DES PICTONS have chosen to step him up to 3m for the first time in this race. That's a sign they think he can stay and can improve for the step up in trip, otherwise surely they would have tried it prior to the big day?! The selection has improved since joining Jamie Snowden's yard and he could have a say here at a decent price.
Won 2 from 4 starts. Upped in trip by Nicky Henderson today to gain even more improvement. The ground should be fine as he's not run on ground quite this quick before. Each way.
Mostly progressive on the whole and has finished second a number of times. Did win last time out and this is a step up in class, but he could take it in his stride. Sam Twiston-Davies rides.

Easy winner of a bumper at Wetherby on racing debut at Wetherby in March of last year. Then won a Novice hurdle over 2m4f at Bewcastle on seasonal return in January. Then finished second in a Novice at Ayr last month. The step up in trip looks likely to suit, and the stable is in good form and won this race in 2023, so a big run could be on the cards at big odds.
Absurd to see Western Knight at such a big price based purely on the unseat last time in my opinion. Will relish the ground and has a great chance here.
Laganhill impressed with wins in novice hurdles at Haydock and Bangor. Though disappointing in Grade 2 company last time, his previous form suggests he could thrive over today's longer trip.

This is a big step up in class, hence the massive price, but he gets the trip as his last run shows when finishing 3rd of 5 over 3m 58yds. Won last May on good ground, so going is not a worry. Interesting that S Bowen, who rode him on that win, returns to the saddle.
Celtic Dino loves this quicker ground and he looks to have a solid chance here. The anticipated fast pace should also suit and his very good conditional jockey is his usual rider.

Hamsiyann has been well backed ahead of this race. Runs off a low mark of 121, carries just 10-02. Maxine O'Sullivan rides and claims a three pounds allowance. Tony Martin is the trainer, well known for his handicap snips. Ran second in the Chester Plate over 2m2f on the turf so obviously has ability. Won a Class 3 handicap hurdle at Cheltenham over 2m5f in November and was well backed into 2-1 favourite that day. So has form in winning handicap hurdles when coming in for market support.
Afadil was third in this last year and looks set to go even closer this time. Tongue strap applied, which it has won with when applied before. Freddie Gingell rides again. EW.

This horse was not on my radar till its last run, but it cantered all over the favorite Balhambar, beating it doing cartwheels. It has been raised 11 pounds, but it seems like the wind operation has paid dividends, and we could see more improvement from this horse today. Travels strongly, so the fast pace predicted should really help.
In what looks like being an open-looking race, I am going to back Alnilam, who should at least place. He is on the back of four great races when winning or placing.
Diamonds For Luck comes into this after three wins on the trot and seems well light with a 7 lbs handy claimer on board for this handicap debut after winning last time out by 17L.

Country Park won his only point but frustratingly has remained a maiden under rules so far in two bumpers and seven hurdle races. Although he has shown promise in his last six races with three 2nd places, a 3rd, and a 4th of 11 last time. In his other race, he looked to be going best, closing behind the leaders when falling two out at Ascot. Benjamin Macey takes off seven pounds to mitigate him being a pound out of the handicap.
Won last time out and goes up 7 lb in the mark. A stone less on the horse's back is another added bonus and can run well here at an each-way price.

Distance winner who won in October and November last year on good and good to soft. Rating went up to 121 from 105 as a result but has run well in class 3 and 2 since. Is a hold-up performer, so could have the race set up for him if today's conditionals/amateurs go too hard from the start.
Has run well in big field handicaps, has won on the ground he is getting today, and won last time out under today's jockey, which I always see as a plus in conditional jockeys' races.

He relishes good ground with a record of 1st, 1st, PU, 2nd on the ground. Despite that, he won on good to soft at Newbury last time out. He was running flat on his pulled-up run at Market Rasen but should be more capable today. He is just 4 lbs higher today and could take advantage of this mark.

Mixed results so far this season, but did land a Premier Handicap at Ascot just before Christmas. Given a short break since a disappointing effort at Newbury last time out, but looks capable of bouncing back here and landing a place at least at a double-figure price, and with many bookies paying out on extra places.

Cormier showed something of a resurgence last time out in first-time cheekpieces, running well under today's jockey to finish 6th in the Morebattle Hurdle. That was just his 2nd start off a 500+ day break, and he seemed to fade at the business end. But with that behind him, he should come on plenty and has been dropped a further 3 lbs. That takes him to a mark of 121, which is 18 lbs below his peak, and he's got plenty of big field handicap form in these conditions, including 4th in a Welsh Champion Hurdle, 7th in a County Hurdle, and 2nd in a Swindon. With headgear retained and the in-form jockey (3 wins in last 11) taking off a further 5 lbs, he's dangerously weighted to outrun his odds.

You’re taking a big risk that she’s ready to go after a big break, but Skelton is hardly an unknown for throwing one in after a lengthy break. 20/1 about a horse with some classy back form is a price I’m happy to take. Her good ground form in and around horses now rated 140+ speaks to a horse well in here off 124 in the context of this race. She’s a forward-going horse who stays further, and Durell's claim is a massive 3lb bonus for a horse that’s never been out of the first 2. 365 is a big outlying price.

Dominic's Fault did win in December by 6L and could be ready for this step up to C2 while just out of the handicap and running well light. With my bookie paying 5P, I think he could be worth an Each Way.
Catch Him Derry runs this distance well on good to soft and has to overcome an eight-pound rise for his last two races: a win at Exeter and a 3rd of 24 at the Cheltenham Festival.

This horse is a real potential improver that is less exposed than virtually all of these and looks to have been put away with this race in mind. The close up third at Newbury behind The New Lion has had the form franked innumerable times and that really does look a cracking effort in the context of this race. The trainer is trying a tongue tie now to squeeze out any further improvement and there could well be an awful lot more to come from this 6yo.

Bo Zenith posted arguably his best effort when a close 2nd in the Grade 1 Juvenile Hurdle here in April 2023, and returned from a 610 break for his new yard last December. Caught the eye that day when rattling home to finish 3rd from a mark of 135 under James Bowen. Hasn't built on that in two starts since, including when disappointing in the Imperial Cup last time, but steps up significantly in trip today which looks a positive based on his running style. Aintree suits those ridden with a bit of patience and the stable reach for cheekpieces to sharpen him up. Reunited with James Bowen from a mark of 136 he should have plenty of scope with conditions to suit.

10/11 aged 6-8. 4/11 favs, 8/11 top 3 in the market. 9/11 carried 11st 5lbs or less, only 4/11 won LTO. Possible he'll find a few of these too classy. However, he has been running fairly well in the big Irish Handicaps with two 2nds and followed that up with a 12L 5th behind Wodhooh in the Martin Pipe. Did well after being outpaced, and we've seen that form get a boost today with Wodhooh going so close against Lossie. Has won on Good, so ground won't be an issue. Mark Walsh now onboard.

8yo gelding who has won twice from 6 starts over hurdles. He recorded a career best RPR of 142 when winning a handicap hurdle at Thurles on his latest start. He will probably need to improve on that effort to overcome his new OR of 140, but he clearly stays well and he should not be inconvenienced by the underfoot conditions.
Won over shorter last time out but beat a decent field there on soft ground, so any rain will help his chance. Step up in trip should suit on breeding.

This race tends to go to horses towards the top end of the market historically. But I want to take a chance on this mare. She's on a decent mark and has a very good 3lbs claiming jockey booked to ride. She's got it all to do in terms of bucking trends. Even the ground would be an issue, but she's a huge price. I just can't let her go unbacked given her overall form. She finished a decent 5th in the Stayers' Hurdle over in Ireland, beaten just 11L by the winner Teahupoo. She had the likes of Asterion Furlonge, Home By The Lee, and Buddy One in front of her. No disgrace there given the caliber of opposition. She ran well last time out. Looked to hold a decent chance before being outpaced over a sharp enough trip, finishing in 5th place, beaten 10L or so. She's unexposed over this distance, so I think she's got an each-way squeak if handling the faster ground.
Lulamba goes up in distance and takes on his elders, but this close 2nd in the Triumph Hurdle should win with his age allowance of ten pounds.

I was shocked that Horaces Pearl did not run in the Supreme as it could have been Fergal's first Cheltenham Festival winner. This horse won at the Aintree Festival last year, and the longer distance will suit. Will be fresh from not running at Cheltenham. My tip of the week. Hoping the horse will prove how good he is. Future World Hurdle horse for next year.

Kappa Jy Pyke has been lightly raced and is therefore open to plenty of improvement. The flatter track here should suit better than Cheltenham and this lightly raced horse looks a solid each way proposition.

CASTLE CARROCK does give the impression he is a big price having caught the eye in Grade 2 novice hurdle company latest. He represents a powerful shrewd British dual-purpose yard and so in a race where an each-way play could be the way to go he appeals.

Maybe better on AW or soft, but he ran okay on GF around here a couple of years ago. Well in, only a pound higher than when just run out of it, having been bumped on his first run for almost a year back in January, and has since won over hurdles.

Mamdoh’s in cracking form, backing up his narrow win at Wolverhampton with a solid second last time off 56. Fast ground is a bit of a question mark, but if he handles it, he’s got every chance of being right there again. Definitely one of the main players if conditions don’t catch him out.

Spitfire Bridge didn’t get much luck last time with a wide trip at Kempton, but had shown better form in his two runs before that. Blinkers go on for the first time which could sharpen him up, he handles quick ground, and the trainer’s got a solid record in turf handicaps (174 runs, 34 wins, 20% strike rate, +52pts @ 30% ROI).
Multiple Jersey winner who ended last season in good form under both codes. Returns from a break but well treated on old form and could go well if ready first time up.
Half-sister to a winner over five furlongs and stable has won the last two runnings of this race. Can extend that record here.
This trainer is more than capable of having them ready first time out so this one who has some good form in the pedigree, could be running well on debut. Drawn well.

A lower draw would have been more ideal so the draw is a concern but horses can run well from this wide draw over this course and distance. Newcomers from this yard often run well first time out, especially over a sprint trip. Small eachway tip for Agent Keen
Tourist manages to squeak into this grade still, despite the good win last time out. Sean Levey is a positive jockey booking, as is the draw at this idiosyncratic course. Great chance at 4/1.

The Steph Hollinshead-trained Pepsi Cat is a C&D winner, has won in this grade and higher, won on G/F, plus she is a pound below her last winning mark. She is top-rated on 86 and has to give weight all around, but this is a big drop in class having bombed out in Listed company LTO. With conditions in her favor and Dougie Costello, who has an excellent record on the 6-year-old mare, winning 5 and placed in 6 from 15 starts, she shouldn't be far away.
Fitness has to be taken on trust as not seen since September. Previous winner on GF ground. Has had obvious training issues, but Cox has retained him, so he must be showing ability at home.

Regal Envoy has shown excellent form on the all-weather during the autumn, winning twice. The 146-day break may have interrupted his momentum, but he has been consistent and appears well handicapped. The drop back to turf is a positive, and he could return to winning ways with a solid performance today.
Was in top shape on the AW until a disappointing last 9 at Wolverhampton in his most recent outing. Overlooking that slip, he'd be a strong contender.

SO SMART is a hardy sprinter with course and distance winning form in hois profile. That makes this ground-versatile six year old interesting allowed to race from his last winning handicap mark , so the thinking is that he is overpriced with his fitness worth taking on trust.

Jacquelina was flying last spring with five wins in quick succession, mostly by getting out in front and staying there. She didn’t quite handle the step up in class late in the season, but she’s back after a break and could easily pick up where she left off if she’s fit. Loves fast ground, goes well fresh, and if she gets her own way up front, she could take a bit of catching.

Royal Accord could go close today with a significant drop in weight and a return to an ideal 5.5f trip, which may play to her strengths. She’s shown enough ability in novice runs to suggest she has a win in her. If settling better and finishing stronger, she’s a live danger to the favourite.

Kameko Spirit’s been knocking on the door, just caught late the last twice after trying to make all, including a solid run with a tongue-tie on for the first time at Wolverhampton. If she brings that form to turf, she’s got a big shout and could be hard to peg back if she gets rolling in front again.
She does have course experience, which should help, and she's now running off the lowest career mark to date, which I hope makes her a serious threat tomorrow if improvements are made.
Finished second, beaten by half a length, in a 7 furlongs handicap at Southwell in his most recent outing. Now stepping up in distance; reliable performer and a strong candidate.
Is well-bred and showed plenty of promise on debut when finishing 2nd at Kempton in January. Improvement likely and every chance of going 1 better.

Soi Dao looks ready to strike after she ran to form last time over 9f at Wolves and hinted at more to come when allowed to dictate. Back at a track she goes well at, down in trip, and now 4lb lower than when placing over C&D last spring before winning next time out, she looks set for a big run.

I've napped Outrace in this race but if that doesn;t come off then surely Monks Mead will hit the jam post instead. The gelding is well at home on this surface and looks ahead of Darvel, King of Speed and Soi Dao. He has never won here but has never failed to be placed on four occasions.

That's For Sure looked a promising recruit for Karl Burke as a juvenile. Close 3rd in a 3-way photo on debut, then followed up with a win on quick ground at Carlisle. Failed to progress after two failed efforts in juvenile sales races and handicaps, was gelded, tried in blinkers and visor without success. Now with a new handler and two recent AW runs from a lower handicap mark have shown more promise, and a return to quick ground could see him get more competitive.

Darvel won a division of this race here last April when returning from a break while running off a 65. Although a bit quiet since, he returns from a break running off a 62 and could be ready to go again.
Received strong support when winning by a head off a mark of 59 over 9 furlongs at Wolverhampton three outings ago; finished fifth, beaten by 2 lengths off a mark of 63. Remains a viable contender.

Outrace is one of those selections that after he wins, you look back and think, 'Oh yeah, should've seen that.' This is what I have seen. He is the fastest horse in the speed ratings over the last six months. He last won in November wearing cheekpieces for the first time. Today, he wears blinkers for the first time. He has appeared at Bath twice, finishing 1st and 2nd. When he won, he was ridden by this jockey and was rated at 69. Today, he is rated at 61. Richard Hannon is the top trainer here in this race. The track has been ventidrained in early March, and last month there was little rainfall, so any rain isn't going to change the surface - this is a big bonus. He has many dangers in the race, which is a good sign as the pace will be strong.
Placed twice in four attempts over course and distance off marks of 56 and 57. Races off 54 today and should be staying on the end following 2 runs over a mile and a quarter.

Baynoona steps up in trip here and is now 15lbs below her opening handicap mark, so she’s starting to look dangerously well treated. Yet to fully fire, but the extra distance might bring out more and she’s definitely one to keep an eye on at this level.

Mrembo was a model of consistency last season and now returns off a 4lb lower mark than her last run. She placed multiple times off higher ratings and looks well treated if tuned up for this. Fitness is the only question, but on form and mark, she’s a major player.

Race 7 at Bath is the DragonBet - Real Bookmakers Handicap (Class 6) for 4-year-olds and upwards over 2,338 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 4-year-old gelding Meet Me In Meraki from the Paul David Evans yard, and will be ridden by Jordan Williams. This son of Twilight Son is a three-time winner and is worth keeping an eye on, with consistency improving as time goes by.
Stayed on inside the final furlong when 3rd over course and distance in August 2023 off a 4-pound higher mark. Comes here race fit following a successful winter campaign on the all-weather.

Ladypacksapunch wasn’t great last time after a slow start but usually needs things to fall right from the back anyway. She’s back from a break now, returns to the scene of her fast-ground win last summer, and is only 1lb above that mark. Yard does alright in spring turf handicaps (123 runs, 12 wins, 10% strike rate, +9pts @ 8% ROI), so she’s not without a chance if things go her way.
Yet to break her maiden, Aquifolia has struggled in previous outings, but with a return to action after a break, she may offer better value at a low mark if showing improvement.

Cast Party has shown promise in both starts so far, especially when a close second at Kempton last time. He took a nice step forward there and looks like there’s more to come. This looks a good spot for him and he should be right in the mix with a big chance of getting off the mark.
Built on his latest debut experience to finish fourth, just a length behind, in a novice race here in his most recent start. Expected to progress more.
Niminy Piminy made a fantastic debut winning without much pressure from the rider 4 months ago so it can be expected to continue its progress today.
Ran well on the all-weather on debut when a neck runner-up over the 7 furlongs. The jockey claims a handy 5 lbs, which should aid this one's chances of breaking its maiden tag.

Captain Parma shaped well on debut when fourth over 8f here, especially considering the support he had in the market. Trainer’s going well, and the drop in trip might help sharpen him up. Should improve plenty for that first run and looks one to keep on side.
Has won his last 5 races over 7f and keeps finding improvement to suggest his ceiling has not yet been reached.

Jimmy Speaking ran a solid race last time over 6f here, staying on strongly to be beaten just a length, and now steps up in trip. He won on seasonal debut last year, so goes well fresh, and if he sees out the extra furlong, he’s got a decent shout again.

Bobby Joe Leg bounced back with a solid win at Newcastle two starts ago off 67 and is still well treated at the weights. Didn’t fire last time, but a return to a more galloping track like this should play to his strengths. Capable of a big run if bouncing back from a below par effort last time out.

Made a stable debut last time out 3 weeks ago, finishing 5/8 after being badly hampered. Has a decent AW record, winning at Kempton on the final run for the previous trainer. Yard goes well at Southwell.

This ex-Eve Johnson-Houghton trained 3-y-o gelding was only beaten a neck behind the George Baker trained Cheeky Stanley on his debut for new trainer P D Evans over six furlongs at Chelmsford City eight days ago. So, able to run from the same mark of 59 and with K Shoemark booked to ride, it looks like a win today.

Daughter of Havana Grey & Mary Stewart ( Dam's sire Dawn Approach ) who was last seen at Newcastle 22 days ago where finishing a nearest finish 5th/9 and most certainly shaped better than that bare result suggests her mark continues to ease here and is now operating on an extremely dangerous mark of 59 now surely it won't be a long wait from this point on for her to get rid off the maiden status and this looks a straightforward assignment that is up to to her level jockey D Nolan takes the ride on David O'meara's inmate bold showing should be expected in attempt to shed the maiden tag must be seriously considered in a race of this nature

Crying out for 5f after fading at the line in the most recent outing over 6f, where he managed to hold onto 3rd in a heavy traffic race. Won his last race over today's trip and before that was running very consistently over 5/6f. Only up 1lb from that last performance and with a favorable draw plus the jockey on board who broke his duck, he has a great chance here.

Lilchita hasn’t shown much on paper but likely needed the run last time and now drops sharply in trip, which could be a sign of intent. Overall form’s not inspiring, but there’s a hint this might be a bit of a plot, and at the prices, she could be worth a small play.

KINGDOM OF TIME is very well bred, a son of Dubawi out of a Galileo mare, he's taken some time to get going but his last 3 runs have been very positive. Up against Paradoxical again tonight having lost by just over a length last time. That horse put in a poor performance just 24 hours ago and I think that gives Archie Watson and Hollie Doyle every chance today.

Las Ramblas ran better than the result suggests when fourth from a poor draw at Nottingham, and she’s got a few things in her favour here. She won on debut, so can go well fresh, and this is her first run since a wind op, which could bring improvement. Back down in trip and not one to rule out if ready to go.
Won here last year at this time of year and ran well here on the comeback LTO from this mark when 3rd behind Cracking Gold. Should strip fitter here back in a Class 4.

Narmar hasn’t quite clicked lately and was below par over 7f here last time, but the step back up in trip could help and he’s now 18lbs below his peak mark. Still trying to find his level, but he’s definitely on a dangerous mark if it all comes together.

5yo gelding who has posted 4 top 3 finishes, including a single victory from 9 starts on synthetic surfaces. His 2 starts over today's course and distance have yielded a win (RPR 89) and a third place finish (RPR 88), which suggests that he remains feasibly treated off his current OR of 80.

Trainer Susan Corbett sends Clear Angel on the 8-hour round trip from her Otterburn stables, 35 miles north of Newcastle. Clear Angel went into my tracker on the 23/3/24 after he didn't get a clear run in the Spring Mile Donny, finishing 6th on soft off 79. Won 2 at Wetherby and Carlisle in 2023. The Dark Angel gelding is returning from a long layoff but has gone well fresh in the past. Has an e/w chance at a nice price.

Epidavros has been in and around the money for all but her first run for a new yard back in July last year. With two wins and three thirds out of six runs, she is worth a chance on this AW debut off a mark of 74 with a 5 lbs claimer in the saddle. Her latest win in September was off a 71 EW 4P.
Two weeks ago, Caballo De Mar completed a hat-trick started at Ayr and continued with 2 races in C&D. It does not seem to have reached its limit, so it can land this at the expense of Humble Spark.

Makes a seasonal reappearance in a much lower class than what he was running in last year. Runs off 82, the same mark as when he was unlucky not to win over course and distance last September. Big chance.

Humble Spark has been on the up this year and looked strong when winning well over 11f here last time. He travelled smoothly and saw it out well, so the extra distance shouldn’t be a problem. Still looks to have more to come and if he keeps improving, he’s got every chance of going close again.
Tempting price to get a place as he was unlucky in running last time and won well on penultimate start. Worth an each-way bet back at Southwell.

Ancient Myth was well beaten at Chester after doing too much early and now returns from a long break with a rise in trip. He’s got a fair bit to prove off this mark but there's probably a bit of each-way value with the books paying 3 places.

Combustion is flying right now, making it four wins on the bounce with a comfortable success at Lingfield off 55. He’s well treated at the weights, has already won over C&D, and is clearly thriving. Still looks to be improving and brings strong credentials to the table again.

Deservedly got off the mark, with a comfortable success over 5 furlongs here in February. Raised 6 lbs for that but has subsequently finished a runner-up over this trip at both Chelmsford and Lingfield. This looks a good opportunity to regain the winning thread.

Race 7 at Southwell today is the Weekly 5 Free Bet With BetUK Handicap (Div 1) (Class 6) for 4-year-olds and upwards over 1,222 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 4-year-old gelding from the Brian Toomey yard, and will be ridden by Warren Fentiman. This son of Exceed and Excel has been in really good form recently and has given the impression that the win is not far off. It should pay to follow here.

Port Hedland is starting to get the hang of things over on the buisness end and looks the way to go here in my point of view was last seen at Wolverhampton 13 days ago where finishing a nearest finish 3rd/7 steps back up in trip here going over the 6 furlong trip that being a positive move by his connections as he hit the line very strongly over the 5 furlong trip last time out now with this extra furlong at his disposal he can have a huge say over on the business end and his current operating mark of 53 is well within his capabilities this class 6 handicap is a lot thinner than it may seen at a quick glance of the form book and A W Carroll's gelded son of Cable Bay can finally get his head in front with jockey Hector Crouch taking the ride that being a positive jockey booking must be taken seriously here

Race 8 at Southwell today is the Weekly 5 Free Bet With BetUK Handicap (Div 1) (Class 6) for 4-year-olds and upwards over 1,222 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 6yo gelding from the D Shaw yard and will be ridden by Joanna Mason. This son of Dabirsim has improved well in recent outings, with jockey Mason getting on well with the gelding a plus. He should be a major player today.

Tough At The Top didn’t land a blow last time after a slow start over 5f here, but steps up in trip and could improve for it. Has had a short break and starts out in handicaps off what looks a fair mark based on earlier form. Needs to step up, but not without a squeak if settling better.

Thunderous Love did too much too soon at Kempton last time but is usually a consistent type and now drops back to what looks her best trip. The yard’s going well and has a good spring turf handicap record (142 runs, 24 wins, 16% strike rate, +123 pts @ 87% ROI), so with a more measured ride she could bounce right back and go well.
